verses.text: Ephraim’s men confronted Gideon: ‘Why did you treat us like this? Why didn’t you call us when you went to fight Midian?’ They came at him hard. 😠
He answered, ‘What have I done compared with you? Isn’t Ephraim’s leftover grape harvest better than Abiezer’s full harvest? 🍇
God put Midian’s commanders Oreb and Zeeb in your hands. What did I do next to that?’ Once he said this, their anger cooled off. 🤝
Gideon reached the Jordan and crossed over with his three hundred men. They were worn out, but still chasing the enemy. 🏃
He asked Succoth’s men, ‘Please give my people some bread. They’re exhausted, and I’m chasing Zebah and Zalmunna, Midian’s kings.’ 🍞
Succoth’s leaders shot back, ‘Do you already have Zebah and Zalmunna in your hands? Why should we feed your army?’ 🙅
Gideon said, ‘When Yahweh hands Zebah and Zalmunna over to me, I’ll come back and punish you with thorns and briers from the wilderness.’ 🌵
From there he went up to Penuel and asked the same thing, but Penuel’s men answered just like Succoth’s had. 🚶
He told Penuel’s men too, ‘When I come back safe, I’ll tear down this tower.’ 🏰
Zebah and Zalmunna were at Karkor with about fifteen thousand men—the survivors of the eastern army. A hundred and twenty thousand armed men had already fallen. ⚔️
Gideon went up by the route of the tent-dwellers, east of Nobah and Jogbehah, and struck the army while they felt secure. 🏕️
Zebah and Zalmunna ran, but Gideon chased them, captured both kings, and threw their whole army into confusion. 🏃
Gideon son of Joash returned from battle by the Heres Pass. 🌄
He captured a young man from Succoth and questioned him. The young man wrote down Succoth’s leaders and elders—seventy-seven men. ✍️
Gideon came back to Succoth and said, ‘Here are Zebah and Zalmunna—the very guys you mocked me about, saying, “Do you have them yet? Why should we give your exhausted men bread?”’ 👀
He took the city elders and disciplined Succoth’s men with thorns and briers from the wilderness. 🌵
He tore down Penuel’s tower and killed the men of that city. ⚠️
Then he asked Zebah and Zalmunna, ‘What were the men you killed at Tabor like?’ They answered, ‘They looked like you—each one had the bearing of a prince.’ 👑
Gideon said, ‘They were my brothers, my mother’s own sons. As Yahweh lives, if you had let them live, I wouldn’t kill you.’ 😔
Then he told Jether, his firstborn, ‘Get up and kill them!’ But the young man didn’t draw his sword; he was afraid because he was still young. 🗡️
Zebah and Zalmunna said, ‘You do it. A man’s strength matches the man himself.’ So Gideon stood up, killed both kings, and took the crescent ornaments from their camels’ necks. ⚔️
Israel’s people told Gideon, ‘Rule over us—you, your son, and your grandson too. You rescued us from Midian!’ 👑
But Gideon said, ‘I won’t rule over you, and my son won’t either. Yahweh will rule over you.’ 🙏
Then Gideon said, ‘I have one request: each of you, give me an earring from your share of the loot.’ The enemy were Ishmaelites, and they wore gold earrings. 💛
They said, ‘We’ll gladly give them.’ They spread out a cloak, and everyone tossed in an earring from his plunder. 🧥
The gold earrings Gideon asked for weighed 1,700 shekels, not counting the crescent ornaments, pendants, purple robes worn by Midian’s kings, or the chains on their camels. ⚖️
Gideon made an ephod from the gold and set it up in his hometown, Ophrah. All Israel turned to worship it there, and it became a trap for Gideon and his family. ⚠️
Midian was brought down before Israel and never raised its head again. The land had peace for forty years while Gideon was alive. 🕊️
Jerub-Baal—Gideon son of Joash—went home and stayed there. 🏠
Gideon had seventy sons of his own, because he had many wives. 👨‍👦
His concubine in Shechem also had a son for him, and Gideon named him Abimelech. 👶
Gideon son of Joash died at a good old age and was buried in his father Joash’s tomb at Ophrah, in Abiezer’s territory. 🕊️
As soon as Gideon died, Israel’s people turned back to worship the Baals and made Baal-Berith their god. 😔
They forgot Yahweh their God—the one who had rescued them from every enemy around them. 💔
They also showed no kindness to Gideon’s family, even though Jerub-Baal—that’s Gideon—had done so much good for Israel. 😞
